title: Introduction to Machine Learning with Examples in Power Systems
text:
Summary
This six-hour Summer School contribution combines lectures on machine-learning fundamentals and their applications in power systems with facilitated group-project tutorials. The cohort comprised 42 undergraduate students from South China University of Technology, Hunan University, and Xi’an Jiaotong University. The teaching moves from problem formulation and core methods to model evaluation, time-series foundation models, and the practical role of data.

title: Introduction to Machine Learning with Examples in Power Systems
text:
Learning aims

Build an accessible foundation in machine learning for students working on energy and power-system problems.
Connect model choices to engineering questions, available data, and appropriate performance measures.
Help project groups turn an initial idea into a defensible machine-learning workflow.

title: Introduction to Machine Learning with Examples in Power Systems
text:
Indicative topics

Electric power-system background and machine-learning applications in the energy sector
Supervised learning: linear regression, logistic regression, neural networks, and support vector machines
Unsupervised learning: principal component analysis and k-means clustering
Model evaluation, underfitting and overfitting, regularisation, hyperparameters, and validation
Time-series foundation models, including Amazon Chronos
Data preparation, data quality, and open energy-system data sources

title: Introduction to Machine Learning for Energy Systems
text:
Module aims
Equip students with a practical ML toolkit for energy-data problems—including forecasting, classification, anomaly detection, and clustering—and the ability to reason about generalisation, model selection, and data quality in real pipelines.

title: Introduction to Machine Learning for Energy Systems
text:
Intended learning outcomes
By the end of the course, students should be able to:

Formulate regression, classification, supervised-learning, and unsupervised-learning tasks in energy systems.
Train and interpret baseline models including linear regression, logistic regression, and support-vector machines.
Apply PCA and k-means for dimensionality reduction, visualisation, and clustering.
Use appropriate regression and classification performance metrics and explain their trade-offs.
Diagnose underfitting and overfitting, explain model capacity, and apply regularisation.
Conduct hyperparameter tuning with correct training, validation, and test splits.
Explain where reinforcement learning is relevant at a high level.
Describe the motivation for foundation models, with emphasis on time-series models such as Chronos.
Identify major energy and weather data sources and assess data-quality risks.

title: Introduction to Machine Learning for Energy Systems
text:
Content outline

ML framing for energy systems: renewables, inverter-dominated grids, operational data, and task taxonomy.
Supervised learning: linear regression, logistic regression, support-vector machines, and practical model fitting.
Unsupervised learning: PCA, k-means, visualisation, and anomaly discovery.
Evaluation and generalisation: MSE, classification metrics, capacity, overfitting, and regularisation.
Special topics: No Free Lunch intuition, time-series foundation models, and energy-data sources such as ENTSO-E and ERA5.

title: Introduction to Machine Learning for Energy Systems
text:
Hands-on tutorial
The open tutorial repository contains:

svm.py — binary classification with an SVM on a non-linearly separable dataset;
pca.py — PCA dimensionality reduction and visualisation;
kmeans+pca.py — k-means clustering followed by a two-dimensional PCA view; and
chronos_example.py — zero-shot energy-price forecasting with Amazon Chronos.

Students can run the examples in Google Colab or locally using NumPy, Matplotlib, scikit-learn, pandas, and chronos-forecasting.

title: Data Science and Digitalisation: Project Teaching
text:
Example project themes

Tracking European electricity data through longitudinal analysis.
Federated digital twins for smart-building management.
Privacy-by-design for data-driven building operation.
Assessing UK decarbonisation through low-carbon technology deployment.
Analysing electric-vehicle use by commercial fleet operators.
Renewable-energy siting, environmental monitoring, and connected-vehicle regulation.

Several projects developed into conference papers and research outputs; selected examples are listed on the Supervision page.

About
text:
I am a Research Associate in the Control and Power Research Group, Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Imperial College London. I work on the UK Electric Power Innovation for a Carbon-free Society Centre (UK-EPICS). I received my PhD in Electrical Engineering from Imperial College London in 2024.
My research focuses on the intersection of machine learning, optimisation, and system dynamics, with a particular focus on efficient, robust, and secure power-system operation and control under uncertainty and high penetrations of renewable energy.

title: PyTorch FX symbolic_trace 学习笔记
text:
torch.fx.symbolic_trace() 可以理解为一次“不使用真实数值的模拟执行”：

FX 为 forward() 的输入创建 Proxy；
使用这些 Proxy 执行原始 forward()；
Proxy 拦截 module、function 和 tensor method 调用；
tracer 将这些操作记录为 Node，形成 Graph；
FX 根据 Graph 生成新的 forward()；
最终返回可执行的 fx.GraphModule。

Tracing 阶段和正常执行阶段的区别如下：








阶段
输入
操作结果




Symbolic tracing
Proxy
创建 graph nodes，不进行真实 tensor 计算


GraphModule runtime
Tensor
执行真实数值计算



Tracing 时，Proxy 是 Node 的 Python 包装器；tracing 完成后，Graph 保存的是 Node。



import torch
from torch import fx, nn

class ResidualMLP(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.linear = nn.Linear(4, 4)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.linear(x) + x

model = ResidualMLP().eval()
x = torch.tensor([[0.2, -0.4, 0.7, 0.1]])
traced = fx.symbolic_trace(model)

with torch.no_grad():
    torch.testing.assert_close(traced(x), model(x))
traced 是一个 fx.GraphModule。它继承自 nn.Module，包含 FX graph、graph 使用的子模块和参数，以及根据 graph 生成的 forward()，所以可以直接执行：
output = traced(x)






属性或方法
用途




traced.graph
FX 中间表示，包含拓扑有序的 nodes


traced.code
FX 根据 graph 生成的 Python forward()


traced.forward
可执行的生成函数


traced.<submodule>
graph 引用的子模块，例如 traced.linear


traced.named_modules()
根模块和所有子模块


traced.named_parameters()
所有 nn.Parameter


traced.state_dict()
parameters 和 persistent buffers


traced.recompile()
修改 graph 后重新生成 forward()



print(traced.graph)
print(traced.code)
print("Modules:", [name for name, _ in traced.named_modules()])
print("Parameters:", [name for name, _ in traced.named_parameters()])
print("State dict:", list(traced.state_dict()))
输出大致为：
graph():
    %x : torch.Tensor [num_users=2] = placeholder[target=x]
    %linear : [num_users=1] = call_module[target=linear](args=(%x,), kwargs={})
    %add : [num_users=1] = call_function[target=operator.add](args=(%linear, %x), kwargs={})
    return add

def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    linear = self.linear(x)
    add = linear + x
    linear = x = None
    return add

Modules: ['', 'linear']
Parameters: ['linear.weight', 'linear.bias']
State dict: ['linear.weight', 'linear.bias']
其中：

Modules 中的 '' 表示根模块 traced，'linear' 表示 traced.linear；
Parameters 包含可训练的 linear.weight 和 linear.bias；
state_dict 包含 parameters 和 persistent buffers。本例没有 buffers，因此键与 Parameters 相同；
生成代码中的 linear = x = None 用于尽早释放不再使用的局部引用，不改变计算结果。




%x : torch.Tensor [num_users=2] = placeholder[target=x]

%x：对名为 x 的 node 输出的引用；
torch.Tensor：来自 forward() 的 Python 类型标注，不是 dtype；
num_users=2：有两个不同的 consumer nodes 使用该输出；
placeholder：该 node 表示模型输入；
target=x：对应 forward(self, x) 中的参数 x。

本例中 x 的两个 consumers 是 linear 和 add：
         linear
        /      \
x -----        add
        \______/
num_users 统计不同 consumer nodes，而不是在参数中出现的总次数。例如 x + x 中，x 在 add.args 出现两次，但 consumer node 只有一个 add。










属性
含义




name
graph 内该次操作的唯一名称


op
FX 的操作类别


target
输入名、attribute path、module path、callable 或 method 名


args
positional arguments，其中的 Node 引用形成 graph edges


kwargs
keyword arguments


users
使用当前 node 输出的 consumer nodes


all_input_nodes
从嵌套 args/kwargs 中提取的所有输入 nodes


meta
shape、dtype、module stack 等附加信息


type
Python type annotation，不是 tensor dtype



可以这样记忆：
target          = 调用什么
args/kwargs     = 输入和调用参数是什么
all_input_nodes = 输入由哪些 nodes 产生
users           = 输出被哪些 nodes 使用
name            = 这一次 graph 操作叫什么
查看全部 nodes：
for node in traced.graph.nodes:
    print(
        "name=", node.name,
        "op=", node.op,
        "target=", node.target,
        "args=", node.args,
        "kwargs=", node.kwargs,
        "inputs=", [value.name for value in node.all_input_nodes],
        "users=", [user.name for user in node.users],
        "meta=", node.meta,
    )



node.op 表示“如何执行”，node.target 进一步说明“具体执行什么”。








op
target 的含义
典型来源




placeholder
forward() 参数名，例如 "x"
forward(self, x)


get_attr
module attribute path，例如 "weight"
parameter、buffer、constant


call_module
submodule path，例如 "block.conv"
self.block.conv(x)


call_function
Python/PyTorch callable，例如 operator.add
a + b、torch.relu(x)


call_method
tensor method 名，例如 "view"
x.view(...)


output
通常是字符串 "output"
return value





对于：
%conv1 = call_module[target=block.conv1](args=(%x,))
target="block.conv1" 是相对于 GraphModule 根对象的子模块地址：
module = traced.get_submodule("block.conv1")
# 等价于 traced.block.conv1
同一个共享 module 可以被调用多次：
name="shared",   target="shared", args=(x,)
name="shared_1", target="shared", args=(y,)
两个 node 的 name 不同，因为它们是两次计算；target 相同，因为它们使用同一个 module 和同一组参数。






PyTorch 写法
op
常见 target




self.relu(x)
call_module
"relu"


torch.relu(x)
call_function
torch.relu


F.relu(x)
call_function
torch.nn.functional.relu


x.relu()
call_method
"relu"


x + y
call_function
operator.add


torch.add(x, y)
call_function
torch.add


x.add(y)
call_method
"add"



对 call_module，通过 traced.get_submodule(node.target) 取得真实 module；对 call_function，target 本身就是 callable。




对于：
y = self.linear(x) + x
FX 记录：
add_node.args == (linear_node, x_node)
意思是 add 的两个输入分别由 linear_node 和 x_node 产生。这里保存的是 Node 引用，不是字符串、Proxy 或真实 Tensor。
反向查看：
set(x_node.users) == {linear_node, add_node}
因此：
node.args  = 我的输入来自谁
node.users = 我的输出被谁使用
all_input_nodes 是对 args/kwargs 的方便展开。例如：
torch.cat([a, b], dim=1)
即使 a_node 和 b_node 嵌套在 list 中，all_input_nodes 仍能返回：
[a_node, b_node]



FX 没有直接提供 traced.inputs 和 traced.outputs。输入是所有 placeholder nodes；返回结构保存在 output node 的 args 中。
input_nodes = [
    node for node in traced.graph.nodes
    if node.op == "placeholder"
]

output_node = next(
    node for node in traced.graph.nodes
    if node.op == "output"
)

print("inputs:", [(node.name, node.target) for node in input_nodes])
print("output structure:", output_node.args[0])
output_node.args[0] 可能是单个 Node，也可能是由 tuple、list 或 dict 组成的多输出结构。



symbolic_trace() 主要捕获操作和连接，通常不会提供完整的 shape 和 dtype。ShapeProp 使用 representative input 执行 graph，并把 tensor_meta 写入每个 node 的 meta：
from torch.fx.passes.shape_prop import ShapeProp

ShapeProp(traced).propagate(x)

for node in traced.graph.nodes:
    tensor_meta = node.meta.get("tensor_meta")
    if tensor_meta is not None:
        print(
            node.name,
            "shape=", tuple(tensor_meta.shape),
            "dtype=", tensor_meta.dtype,
        )
需要区分：
node.type                  = Python type annotation，例如 torch.Tensor
node.meta["tensor_meta"]  = 实际传播得到的 tensor metadata
tensor_meta.dtype          = 实际 dtype，例如 torch.float32



FX 无法直接处理依赖 tensor 数值的 Python control flow：
def forward(self, x):
    if x.sum() > 0:
        return self.a(x)
    return self.b(x)
Tracing 时 x.sum() > 0 仍然是 Proxy，没有真实值，Python if 无法决定分支，因此通常抛出 TraceError。
普通 Python 常量操作会在 tracing 时直接执行。例如：
constant = 2 + 3
y = x * constant
graph 通常只记录 x * 5，不会为 2 + 3 创建 node。



def summarize_fx(graph_module: fx.GraphModule) -> None:
    for node in graph_module.graph.nodes:
        tensor_meta = node.meta.get("tensor_meta")
        raw_shape = getattr(tensor_meta, "shape", None)
        shape = tuple(raw_shape) if raw_shape is not None else None

        print(
            f"{node.name:12} "
            f"op={node.op:13} "
            f"target={str(node.target):24} "
            f"inputs={[value.name for value in node.all_input_nodes]} "
            f"users={[user.name for user in node.users]} "
            f"shape={shape}"
        )


summarize_fx(traced)
最值得优先查看的属性是：
op      → 这是什么类别的操作？
target  → 具体调用什么？
args    → 输入和参数是什么？
users   → 输出流向哪里？
meta    → tensor 的 shape、dtype 等信息是什么？

title: An Open-Source Toolbox for Embedding Neural Stability Surrogates in Stability-Constrained Optimization
text:
Summary
This guest lecture introduces an open workflow for learning a neural surrogate of small-signal stability and embedding that surrogate as an exact constraint in unit commitment. It was delivered at the third International Summer School on IBR-Dominated Power Systems, held at the University of Strathclyde in Glasgow. The school follows earlier editions at Imperial College London in 2024 and Tsinghua University in 2025.
The accompanying tutorial uses a compact IEEE 14-bus example. It generates eigenvalue-labelled operating points, trains a small residual ReLU network, converts the trained model into mixed-integer linear constraints, and compares baseline and stability-constrained decisions.

title: An Open-Source Toolbox for Embedding Neural Stability Surrogates in Stability-Constrained Optimization
text:
Course materials


Python tutorial Open the GitHub repository


NCET package Documentation · Install

title: An Open-Source Toolbox for Embedding Neural Stability Surrogates in Stability-Constrained Optimization
text:
Tutorial workflow
The notebooks follow the modelling steps in order:

Run AC power flow, dynamic initialisation, and small-signal eigenvalue analysis with ANDES.
Train a residual ReLU regressor in PyTorch to predict the critical eigenvalue real part.
Encode the trained network as mixed-integer linear constraints with NCET.
Solve the baseline and stability-constrained one-period unit commitment problems in CVXPY.

title: Machine Learning and Data Science for Power Systems
text:
Learning outcomes
By the end of the module, students should be able to:

Distinguish supervised and unsupervised learning tasks.
Implement and tune linear regression, logistic regression, support-vector machines, principal-component analysis, and k-means.
Evaluate models using MSE, F1, TPR, FPR, FNR, and TNR.
Diagnose generalisation, overfitting, model capacity, and regularisation.
Conduct hyperparameter tuning with an appropriate validation pipeline.
Explain the role of time-series foundation models and use pretrained models such as Amazon Chronos for energy forecasting.

title: Machine Learning and Data Science for Power Systems
text:
Indicative topics

ML for power systems: data-driven and model-driven approaches; operational use cases.
Supervised learning: linear and logistic regression; support-vector machines.
Unsupervised learning: principal-component analysis and k-means.
Performance assessment: regression and classification metrics.
Generalisation: capacity, bias–variance trade-offs, and regularisation.
Model selection: train/validation/test splits and grid search.
Special topics: No Free Lunch intuition, foundation models, time-series forecasting, and energy-data sources.
